name: A tavern
description: The sign, the room, the keeper, and tonight's trouble. Four lines from one roll.

tables.name: A tavern
tables.description: Roll it when the party goes looking for a drink.

entries.body: The Drowned Cat.
The Lantern and Ladle.
The Second Chance.
The Hanged Goose.
The Low Tide.
The Widow's Kettle.
The Crooked Mile.
The Salt and Candle.
The Three Sisters.
The Copper Fish.
The Quiet Room, which is not.
The Last Oar.
The Broken Bell.
The Sleeping Judge.
The Nine Cups.
The Fox in Boots.
The Harbour Light.
The Old Customs House, now a bar.
The Hen and Halberd.
The Wrong Door.

tables.name: A tavern: the room
tables.description: What the party sees from the door.

entries.body: Low beams, a fire too big for the room, and a dog asleep across the threshold.
Long tables, a loud card game, and sawdust that needed changing yesterday.
Nearly empty. One regular at the bar who turns to look and does not turn back.
Packed to the walls for a wake. Everyone is crying or singing.
Clean, bright, and priced for people who are not the party.
A cellar room down six steps, with the tide audible through the floor.
Stools around barrels, a fiddler, and a cat that owns the place.
Two rooms: one for guards, one for everybody else. Nobody says which is which.
A courtyard under a vine, lanterns, and the smell of something roasting.
Dark, with a single candle per table and a rule about voices.
Warm, damp, and full of fishermen arguing about a boat.
An upstairs room reached by a ladder, with the best view in town.
Kept by a broad, quiet woman who remembers every face and every debt.
Kept by a retired sailor with one story and twelve versions of it.
Kept by twins who finish each other's insults.
Kept by a man far too well dressed for the place, and nervous about it.
Kept by a girl of fourteen, because her father is upstairs and unwell.
Kept by an old priest who left the temple and took the incense with him.
Kept by somebody who will not give a name and does not need to.
Kept by a cheerful giant who cannot count change.
Kept by a widow who waters the ale and everyone knows and nobody minds.
Kept by a former guard who still stands like one.
Kept by a cook, mostly. The bar is an afterthought and the food is not.
Kept by nobody tonight. Help yourself and leave the coin on the bar.

tables.name: A tavern: tonight's trouble
tables.description: What happens if the party stays an hour.

entries.body: Tonight: somebody is looking for a fight and has chosen the wrong table.
Tonight: a stranger buys the whole room a round and asks one question.
Tonight: the guard come in, count heads, and leave.
Tonight: a purse goes missing, and the door is barred until it is found.
Tonight: a song starts that everyone knows and the party does not.
Tonight: the keeper asks the party, quietly, to walk somebody home.
Tonight: a debt collector reads a name off a list, and it is one of the party's.
Tonight: the cellar floods, slowly.
Tonight: an old friend of one of the party is here, and pretends not to be.
Tonight: a game of cards, played for a favour instead of coin.
Tonight: nothing. It is a good night, and the party will remember it.
Tonight: the fire goes out and nobody can relight it.
